title: The Alibi of Ashcombe
premise: Estate lawyer Ivo Kavanagh is summoned to the decaying seaside town of Ashcombe to probate the will of Edith Marlowe, a woman who vanished thirty years ago and was declared dead in absentia. The will is legally impossible — and it arrives with her diary, whose entries continue for two years after her disappearance, written in a hand that grows increasingly frightened. As Ivo follows the diary through Ashcombe's tangled memories, he discovers Edith witnessed a crime committed by men who now run the town, faked her own vanishing to protect her daughter, and lived hidden until someone finally found her. The ending: Ivo exposes the surviving conspirator using the diary's coded final entry as evidence outside the courtroom's reach, granting Edith posthumous justice while choosing to let her daughter keep the peaceful lie of a mother who simply left.
about_author: Sebastian Okonkwo is a former legal clerk turned novelist who spent a decade handling probate files in coastal England, where he collected the strange, half-finished stories the dead leave behind. He writes quiet mysteries about paperwork, memory, and the violence that respectable towns prefer to forget.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ivo Kavanagh receives an envelope containing Edith Marlowe's will, dated eleven years after she vanished. POV Ivo. He travels to fog-bound Ashcombe, unsettled by the document's impossible date and the firm's insistence he handle it personally. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Ivo meets solicitor Ruth Adeyemi, executor of the will, who warns him the town agreed long ago on its version of Edith's story. POV Ivo. Locals are polite but evasive; the pub goes quiet at her name. Emotional beat: the first sense of a conspiracy of silence.

chapters.title: The Diary's First Lie
chapters.summary: Ivo begins reading Edith's recovered diary; entries continue past her disappearance date, describing a life in hiding. POV Ivo, with diary excerpts in Edith's voice. He realizes either the diary is forged or the town buried a living woman. Emotional beat: vertigo — the ground truth shifting beneath him.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Buried an Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Ivo tracks down Nell Marlowe, Edith's daughter, now a hospice nurse who refuses to discuss the memorial service held over an empty grave. POV Nell. She insists her mother abandoned them and begs Ivo to drop it. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into denial.

chapters.title: Three Men and a Boathouse
chapters.summary: Diary entries from thirty years ago describe Edith witnessing something at the old boathouse the night before she vanished. POV Ivo. He visits the derelict site and finds fresh footprints — someone else is reading the same trail. Emotional beat: dread of being watched.

chapters.title: The Alibi Committee
chapters.summary: Ivo uncovers that three prominent men — harbourmaster Colm Voss, retired doctor Peter Lyle, and developer Aubrey Fenn — each provided alibis for one another the night Edith disappeared. POV Ivo. Two are dead; Fenn now owns half of Ashcombe. Emotional beat: the shape of the cover-up emerging.

chapters.title: What Edith Saw
chapters.summary: A 1994 diary passage reveals Edith saw the three men drown a young drifter, Danny Quill, whose death was ruled accidental. POV alternating Ivo and Edith's diary voice. She wrote everything down — then stopped writing in this notebook and started another. Emotional beat: horror arriving quietly, in ink.

chapters.title: Nell Breaks
chapters.summary: Ivo confronts Nell with the murder revelation; she admits her mother sent her letters from hiding for two years, which she burned after threats against her family. POV Nell. Her denial cracks into fury. Emotional beat: guilt transformed into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Second Notebook
chapters.summary: Ruth reveals the will's condition: the estate passes only if the truth of Edith's death is established. She hints the second notebook exists and Fenn wants it destroyed. POV Ruth. Someone ransacks Ivo's lodgings overnight. Emotional beat: the stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Colm Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews dying, morphine-hazed Colm Voss, who half-confesses to the night at the boathouse and names the person who helped Edith disappear: his own sister. POV Ivo. Voss dies hours later of an apparent overdose. Emotional beat: answers arriving exactly too late.

chapters.title: The Sister in the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Ivo finds Maren Voss, the former lighthouse keeper who sheltered Edith, now elderly and unafraid. POV Maren. She confirms Edith lived under a false name until eleven years ago — when someone came asking questions, and Edith fled again. Emotional beat: tenderness inside a hard story.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Maren recounts Edith's last visit: she'd been recognized by a photograph in Fenn's development brochure and knew they'd come back to finish it. POV Maren, framed by Ivo. The trail goes cold at a bus station. Emotional beat: hope narrowing to a single thread.

chapters.title: Peter Lyle's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo breaks into the dead doctor's sealed office and finds hush-money payments recorded for decades — including one made eleven years ago, after Edith resurfaced. POV Ivo. The payment's recipient is listed only as 'N.M.' Emotional beat: betrayal — the money went somewhere unthinkable.

chapters.title: Nell's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ivo confronts Nell: she took Fenn's money years ago to pay her husband's debts, believing she was selling silence about nothing. POV Nell. Devastated, she remembers a detail she suppressed — the address where she once posted a reply letter. Emotional beat: complicity and redemption colliding.

chapters.title: The Cottage Above the Cliffs
chapters.summary: Following Nell's memory, Ivo finds the isolated cottage where Edith lived her final months. Inside: the second notebook, hidden in a wall, its final pages coded. POV Ivo. A car turns into the lane behind him. Emotional beat: triumph interrupted by pursuit.

chapters.title: Fenn Explains Himself
chapters.summary: Aubrey Fenn corners Ivo, urbane and menacing, offering partnership: bury the diary, take the fee, let Ashcombe keep its peace. POV Ivo. Fenn admits to the cover-up but claims Edith died naturally and the 'murder' is her invention. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as reason.

chapters.title: Decoding Edith
chapters.summary: Ivo and Nell crack the cipher — a childhood game between mother and daughter — revealing Edith's account of being hunted and her final entry naming where she hid the original evidence. POV alternating Ivo and decoded Edith. Emotional beat: a dead woman speaking clearly at last.

chapters.title: The Tide Cave
chapters.summary: The evidence — Danny Quill's belongings and Edith's sworn recording — is cached in a cave accessible only at low tide. Ivo retrieves it as Fenn's man closes in; a violent struggle leaves Ivo injured but the recordings intact. POV Ivo. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Knowing Fenn owns the police and half the courts, Ivo bypasses them: he broadcasts the recording at the town's centenary gathering and distributes copies to national press before Fenn can suppress it. POV Ivo, with townspeople's reactions. Emotional beat: catharsis — a town forced to remember together.

chapters.title: Ashcombe After
chapters.summary: Fenn is arrested as the story detonates nationally; old residents begin giving statements they withheld for thirty years. POV Ruth. Danny Quill's family receives his remains and an apology decades late. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, but arriving.

chapters.title: The Empty Grave, Refilled
chapters.summary: Edith is reburied beside her real history, her headstone rewritten with the truth. Nell chooses not to prosecute the memory of her mother's deception, keeping the lie that kept her safe as a private mercy. POV Nell. Emotional beat: forgiveness without forgetting.

chapters.title: Ivo's Own Alibi
chapters.summary: Leaving Ashcombe, Ivo mails the completed probate — the will executed, the condition fulfilled — and keeps one blank page of Edith's diary as a reminder that paper outlives power. POV Ivo. He reflects that belonging sometimes means carrying a town's worst secret honestly. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
